articles.title_zh: Spanish pensioner whose eviction sparked nationwide protests dies, union says
facts_zh:
Spanish pensioner whose eviction sparked nationwide protests dies, union says
- Published
An elderly woman whose eviction sparked nationwide protests over Spain's housing crisis and a political row that triggered early elections has died, according to Madrid's tenants union.
Maricarmen Abascal, 87, was forcibly removed on a stretcher from her apartment of more than 70 years on 23 September after she was unable to afford rent increases.
The company that owned the flat later offered to allow her to return at a lower rate - but she was unable to sign an agreement as she had been admitted to hospital.

all_titles.en: Spanish pensioner whose eviction sparked nationwide protests dies, union says

articles.title_zh: Chinese runner dropped by sponsor after riding bike during marathon
facts_zh:
Chinese runner dropped by sponsor after riding bike during marathon
- Published
A Chinese fitness influencer has been dropped by her sponsor after she apologised for riding a bicycle during the Berlin marathon.
Sun Yuanyuan, known as Abeeeer on Chinese social media, had claimed a personal best during the event which was held in September.

But an Instagram page dedicated to monitoring inaccurate or misleading race times posted by influencers published a picture which appeared to show Sun on a bicycle between the 35km and and 40km marks.

all_titles.en: Chinese runner dropped by sponsor after riding bike during marathon

articles.title_original: Israelis mourn 7 October attack victims three years after deadly Hamas raid
articles.title_zh: Israelis mourn 7 October attack victims three years after deadly Hamas raid
facts_zh:
Israelis mourn 7 October attack victims three years after deadly Hamas raid
- Published
Memorial events have taken place in Israel on the third anniversary of the devastating Hamas-led attack there that sparked the war in Gaza.
Families paid tribute to their loved ones at some of the sites where about 1,200 people were killed in the assault and 251 were taken hostage.

"The nation unites on this day in the longing for our dear ones," said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faced calls from protesters for an independent state inquiry into security failures that day.

all_titles.en: Israelis mourn 7 October attack victims three years after deadly Hamas raid

articles.title_zh: Canada to indefinitely bar mental illness as sole reason for access to euthanasia
facts_zh: Legislation is an effort by ruling Liberals to address growing clash over who has access to doctor-assisted death Canada ’s federal government said on Wednesday it would advance legislation to prevent people whose sole health condition is mental illness from accessing euthanasia, an effort by the ruling Liberal party to address a clash in the country over who has access to physician-assisted death.
Under the current rules, people whose sole underlying medical condition is a mental illness have been barred from accessing medical assistance in dying (Maid) to end their lives.
But that ban – due to be lifted in March – has divided lawmakers over whether to permit this expansion of the Maid program.

all_titles.en: Canada to indefinitely bar mental illness as sole reason for access to euthanasia

Trump to speak to Putin about plague lab worker's death in Russia

US President Donald Trump says he has a call set up with Vladimir Putin about the death of a lab worker at a plague research centre in Siberia.
Russian officials say they are investigating the death of the 28-year-old employee and have not confirmed that the suspected disease is pneumonic plague.
They insist there is no risk of an epidemic.

articles.title_original: Children killed while they slept as Russian missile kills 19 in block of flats
articles.title_zh: Children killed while they slept as Russian missile kills 19 in block of flats
facts_zh:
Children killed while they slept as Russian missile kills 19 in block of flats
- Published
A Russian missile has killed 19 people including five children in an apartment block in northern Ukraine, destroying 30 flats as families slept.
Three of the children were one-year-olds in the attack on Pryluky, east of Kyiv, early on Wednesday, and one of the boys died with his mother and grandmother, officials said.
Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky said it was one of Russia's "most vile strikes", and suggested the Russian military had carried it out as a "birthday gift" to Vladimir Putin, who turned 74 on Wednesday.

all_titles.en: Children killed while they slept as Russian missile kills 19 in block of flats

articles.title_zh: France halts use of stun grenades after boy's hand blown off in student protests
facts_zh:
France halts use of stun grenades after boy's hand blown off in student protests
- Published
France has suspended the use of stun grenades for policing student protests that have swept the country, after a 15-year-old's hand was blown off earlier this week.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said he had requested the pause until the facts of Monday's incident in Lens had been "clarified", with conflicting accounts offered by protesters and officials.
The disruption continued on Wednesday with more than 500 schools fully or partially shut.

all_titles.en: France halts use of stun grenades after boy's hand blown off in student protests

articles.title_zh: Canada suspends plans to expand assisted dying to people with mental illness
facts_zh:
Canada suspends plans to expand assisted dying to people with mental illness
- Published
Canada says it will indefinitely suspend plans to expand its medically assisted dying law to people whose sole condition is mental illness, citing a lack of consensus on who would be eligible.
It comes after a parliamentary panel earlier this year recommended that medically assisted dying - known as Maid in Canada - should not be expanded.
On Wednesday, Canada's justice minister, Sean Fraser, said that "while there is not a perfect consensus on this issue, we believe this is the correct approach at this particular time".

all_titles.en: Canada suspends plans to expand assisted dying to people with mental illness

It was there, shortly after 07:00 on 7 October 2023, that Hamas-led attackers killed half the community's 14-member civil defence squad.

Ten people linked to Kenya's first-ever Ebola case quarantined as screening concerns grow
- Published
Ten people who came into contact with a man who died of Ebola in Kenya have been quarantined, health officials in the East African nation say.
They are also trying to trace 57 other contacts of the Kenyan patient after he travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo, dying in hospital in Nairobi on Monday.
This is the East African nation's first-ever Ebola case and there is now growing concern about the country's screening measures.

articles.title_original: Separatists win in Quebec – but does that bring separation from Canada any closer?
articles.title_zh: Separatists win in Quebec – but does that bring separation from Canada any closer?
facts_zh: Lack of majority for Parti Québécois puts any referendum in doubt, especially amid bruising trade war with Trump The victory of the Parti Québécois in Monday’s election in Quebec might seem to bring its signature goal, of separating the French-speaking province from Canada, much closer – but Canadian unity may not be nearly as threatened as may first seem.
The PQ’s victory was both impressive and disappointing.
The party added 56 seats to its roster and more than doubled its vote share compared with the 2022 election, giving it its first taste of power in 14 years.

all_titles.en: Separatists win in Quebec – but does that bring separation from Canada any closer?

articles.title_original: How did Christa Pike survive two lethal injections - and what happens now?
articles.title_zh: How did Christa Pike survive two lethal injections - and what happens now?
facts_zh: How did Christa Pike survive two lethal injections - and what happens now?

- Published
Convicted murderer Christa Pike has woken up and begun speaking from her hospital bed almost a week after authorities in the US state of Tennessee botched her execution, her lawyers said.
Pike, 50, was sent to hospital after surviving two attempts to execute her via lethal injection for the 1995 murder of a 19-year-old she met at a summer camp for troubled teens.

all_titles.en: How did Christa Pike survive two lethal injections - and what happens now?

articles.title_original: Sri Lanka's ex-first lady arrested over alleged misuse of children's hospital donations
articles.title_zh: Sri Lanka's ex-first lady arrested over alleged misuse of children's hospital donations
facts_zh:
Sri Lanka's ex-first lady arrested over alleged misuse of children's hospital donations
- Published
Sri Lanka's former first lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa has been arrested over allegations that a charity she is linked to misused donations raised for a children's hospital.
Anti-corruption authorities arrested the 73-year-old wife of former President Mahinda Rajapaksa at their Colombo home on Wednesday.

They are questioning her over the 10 million rupees ($30,300; £22,800) of donations collected by the Siriliya Saviya charity, meant to be spent on a specialised scanner for Colombo's Lady Ridgeway Children's Hospital.

all_titles.en: Sri Lanka's ex-first lady arrested over alleged misuse of children's hospital donations

articles.title_zh: California pair charged with abusing at least 14 surrogate-born children
facts_zh:
California pair charged with abusing at least 14 surrogate-born children
- Published
A California pair has been charged with multiple counts of abusing at least 14 surrogate-born children - some as young as two months old - and dissuading a witness.
"The number of children who were subjected to this alleged horrific abuse is unprecedented," Los Angeles District Attorney Nathan J Hochman said in a statement.
Guojun Xuan and Silvia Zhang, who US media describe as a couple, were arrested at their Arcadia mansion on Tuesday.

articles.title_original: Oscar-winning actress Eva Marie Saint dies aged 102
articles.title_zh: Oscar-winning actress Eva Marie Saint dies aged 102
facts_zh:
Oscar-winning actress Eva Marie Saint dies aged 102
- Published
Eva Marie Saint, the Oscar-winning actress who starred in Hollywood classics such as On the Waterfront and North by Northwest, has died aged 102.

Saint won the Academy Award for best supporting actress for her movie debut in director Elia Kazan's 1954 crime drama, On the Waterfront; playing Edie Doyle, the moral compass of the film and love interest of Marlon Brando's conflicted boxer-turned-docker.
Five years later, she portrayed femme fatale Eve Kendall, dangerously seducing Cary Grant's entangled advertising executive in Alfred Hitchcock's spy thriller, North by Northwest.

all_titles.en: Oscar-winning actress Eva Marie Saint dies aged 102
